short: Parliament passed legislation declaring Henry VIII the Supreme Head of the Church of England.
full:
On 3 November 1534, the English Parliament passed the Act of Supremacy, legally formalising King Henry VIII's break with the Roman Catholic Church. The landmark legislation declared the king and his successors as the only supreme head on earth of the Church of England, granting him full jurisdictional authority over its doctrines, high appointments, and immense revenues without papal interference.

The legislation legally codified the English Reformation, severing centuries of entrenched papal jurisdiction. It enabled Henry to dissolve the monasteries and appropriate their wealth, while a companion Treason Act made any denial of his absolute supremacy an offence punishable by death. This structural and theological change permanently altered the balance of power between church and state in England.
